proof.text: For the covariant statement set $\mathcal B=\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use right $\mathcal B$-modules. Explicitly a right action corresponds to the left $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-action $a^{\mathrm{op}}m=(-1)^{|a||m|}ma$; the Koszul sign makes the differentials and compositions agree. This equivalence preserves graded splittings, dg submodules, coproducts, shifts and representables. Thus the filtration of [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] becomes the covariant enriched free-module filtration for [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model].

proof.text: Specialize [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model] to $\mathcal N=\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$. Its projective structure is generated by the enriched free maps $\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes i$, where $i$ ranges over the sphere-to-disk generating cofibrations $S^{n+1}\to D^n$ of complexes. Under the module convention of Step 1 these are precisely representable sphere-to-disk maps, and their right lifting class is the objectwise trivial fibrations. Denote this set of module maps by $I$.

source.place: Toën, §3, generating maps in the projective enriched diagram model

proof.text: Fix $P_i\subset P_{i+1}$ with quotient $\bigoplus_\alpha h_{U_\alpha}[n_\alpha]$. Put $s_\alpha=-n_\alpha$: the shifted unit has degree $s_\alpha$, not $n_\alpha$. A graded section lifts it to $e_\alpha$. Units are closed, so $d e_\alpha\in P_i(U_\alpha)^{s_\alpha+1}$ and $d^2e_\alpha=0$. Write $F_U(K)$ for the enriched free right module on $K$ at $U$, corresponding under Step 1 to the enriched free diagram. It is $K\otimes h_U$, or $h_U\otimes K$ via graded symmetry. The closed element $d e_\alpha$ defines $F_{U_\alpha}(S^{s_\alpha+1})\to P_i$. Push out the coproduct of these maps along $F_{U_\alpha}(S^{s_\alpha+1})\to F_{U_\alpha}(D^{s_\alpha})$. The resulting module $Q$ has graded module $P_i^\#\oplus\bigoplus_\alpha h_{U_\alpha}[n_\alpha]^\#$ and new generators $t_\alpha$ with $d(t_\alpha a)=(d e_\alpha)a+(-1)^{s_\alpha}t_\alpha d a$. Indeed maps out of this module are exactly an old dg map and chosen generator images with differential the prescribed attaching cycles, which is the pushout universal property. The map $Q\to P_{i+1}$ sends $t_\alpha a$ to $e_\alpha a$. It is a graded isomorphism by the chosen section, and a chain map by the displayed Leibniz formula, hence a dg isomorphism. Thus the inclusion is the asserted generating-cell pushout. No basis for the abelian groups $\mathcal B(V,U)$ or flatness hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: The exhaustive sequence, with endpoint $P_\omega=P$, is continuous: the union of dg submodules is their colimit, since compatible maps define a unique map on their union. Step 3 therefore makes $0\to P$ an $I$-cell map by the definition in [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization]. For cofibrancy use only lifting closure, not that node's small-object factorization theorem. Put $T=I^{\pitchfork}$, the objectwise trivial fibrations by [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Each map in $I$ lifts against $T$ by definition. A coproduct of such maps lifts componentwise. Its pushouts lift by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Apply [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] to the continuous chain indexed by $0\leq i\leq\omega$ to conclude $0\to P\in{}^{\pitchfork}T$. The enriched projective model identifies this class with the cofibrations. No domain-smallness assumption is invoked here.

proof.text: By definition of cofibrancy, an object is cofibrant when its initial map is a cofibration. Therefore $P$ is projectively cofibrant. The argument also covers the empty coproduct and the zero filtration: the initial map $0\to0$ is an isomorphism and hence a cofibration, while finite filtrations are treated as continuous chains with identity stages. Reversing the dg category returns the asserted covariant-module formulation.

title: Semi-free dg modules are projectively cofibrant
statement: Use dg modules and semi-free filtrations as defined in [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement], with the projective model structure and enriched free sphere-to-disk generating cofibrations of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]; for covariant modules apply the right-module convention to the opposite dg category. In the projective model structure on covariant dg modules over a small dg category, whose generating cofibrations are the enriched free modules on the sphere-to-disk cofibrations of chain complexes, every semi-free dg module is projectively cofibrant. More precisely, for a semi-free module with graded-split filtration $0=P_0\subset P_1\subset\cdots$ and successive quotients coproducts of shifts of representables, each inclusion $P_i\to P_{i+1}$ is a pushout of a coproduct of enriched free sphere-to-disk generating cofibrations, and the union $0\to P$ is a relative cell map.
